uncited: All methods in this family operate on the principle that a continuous function $V(\mathbf{p})$ must be approximated from a discrete set of samples $V_i$ located at grid positions $\mathbf{p}_i$.
**Query Positioning**: Determining the 3D coordinate $\mathbf{p}$ along the ray $r(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ where a value is needed.
This may involve converting depth parameters to physical distances or warping coordinates for neural encodings.
**Kernel/Weight Application**: Computing weights $w_i(\mathbf{p})$ based on the distance between $\mathbf{p}$ and the sample centers $\mathbf{p}_i$.
Linear interpolation uses a triangular kernel with support over two adjacent voxels.
It provides a balance between computational speed and smoothness.
Quadratic re-sampling employs a kernel with support over three voxels.
Cubic-spline interpolation uses a kernel with support over four voxels, offering higher-order continuity.
This is not a kernel itself, but a specific evaluation method and application of interpolation functions for determining the position of a 1D step edge.
Re-sample discrete samples across the step using an interpolation function.
Compute the mean of the grey-values on the low and high sides of the step.
